newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP thinks stock tax to be scrapped by FY99--paper.
newsitem.headline: LDP thinks stock tax to be scrapped by FY99--paper.

text.p: A Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) tax panel believes Japan's securities transaction tax should be abolished in fiscal 1999/00 at the latest to stimulate securities trade, a Japanese business daily said on Tuesday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the panel also believes the government should impose a heavier capital gains tax on individual investors to spread the tax burden more fairly.
The LDP panel will discuss the details later this year before drafting its conclusions for consideration as part of the government's tax reform plans, the newspaper said.
The panel is considering two time frames for when the government should scrap the securities transaction tax, the newspaper said.
Ending the tax in 1998/99 was one option, but the panel thought this would sharply reduce government tax revenue and possibly affect Japan's fiscal reforms, the paper said.
It said the other time frame the panel is considering is one allowing the government to reduce the tax rate in fiscal 1998/99 before abolishing it completely in 1999/00.
